newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil government sees exports rising in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil government sees exports rising in 1997.

text.p: Brazilian exports should improve in 1997 and beyond because of a conjunction of favourable factors, said Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.
Cortes, announcing total 1996 exports of $47.746 billion, said Brazilian industry was building up its export potential.
He listed record foreign direct investment in 1996 of about $8.0 billion and surging capital goods imports, up 12.6 percent in 1996 over 1995, as foundation stones for future exports.
"Together, (they) are certainly indicative of greater export capacity in the medium to long-term," Cortes told reporters.
Cortes also said that, according to OECD figures, average world economic growth in 1997 would rise to 2.5 percent from 2.0 percent in 1996.
"This signifies an increase in international demand which should be favourable for Brazilian overseas sales," he said.

On the internal front, Cortes said steps taken by the government, such as tax exemption for raw materials and semi-manufactured goods, the revival of an export credit insurance agency and special credit lines for exporters, should raise exports in 1997.
"The tax exemption will really only have an effect when the harvest starts (in March)," he said, referring to Brazil's primary commodities, such as coffee, soybeans, sugar and others.
"The primary objective (of the measures) is to create competitive conditions for Brazilian firms that are as close as possible to those enjoyed by their international competitors," he added.
